units.source_text: 夕雾吟唱“右将军墓草初青”之诗。

en.t: Yugiri chanted the poem, The grass on the Right General's grave has just turned green.

units.source_text: 右大将藤原保忠夭死，乃近世之事。

en.t: The early death of the Right Major Captain Fujiwara no Yasutada was an event of more recent times.

units.source_text: 可知不论古今，人世必有伤逝之痛。

en.t: This shows that in every age, old or new, human life must include the pain of mourning the dead.

units.source_text: 而于柏木尤甚：不论身份高下，无人不扼腕叹惜。

en.t: In Kashiwagi's case the grief was especially intense: high and low alike, everyone wrung their hands and lamented his loss.

units.source_text: 只因此人不但学问渊博，且又异常重情，

en.t: For he was not only deeply learned, but also unusually rich in feeling,

units.source_text: 所以连平素不甚亲近的僚属，以及老年的侍女，也都恋慕悲伤。

en.t: and so even colleagues who had not been especially close to him, as well as elderly gentlewomen, mourned him with affection and longing.

units.source_text: 皇上尤深惋惜，每逢举行管弦之会，

en.t: The Emperor felt his loss most deeply, and whenever a gathering of music was held,

units.source_text: 总首先想起柏木，不胜感慨。

en.t: he always thought first of Kashiwagi and was overcome with emotion.

units.source_text: “惜哉卫门督！”变成了当时通行的一句话，无人不说。

en.t: What a pity about the Captain of the Gate Guards! became a common saying of the time, and everyone repeated it.

units.source_text: 源氏怜惜柏木，日久愈深。

en.t: Genji's pity and regret for Kashiwagi only deepened as the days went by.

units.source_text: 只有他一人心中知道薰君这孩子是柏木的遗孤，

en.t: He alone knew in his heart that the child Kaoru was Kashiwagi's orphaned son,

units.source_text: 而别人却是做梦也想不到的，所以也是枉然。

en.t: but no one else would ever dream of it, and so his knowledge was useless.

units.source_text: 到了秋天，薰君已会扶床学步，其可爱之状难于形容。

en.t: By autumn, Kaoru could already pull himself up by the bed and practice walking, and his charm was beyond description.

units.source_text: 源氏不但在人前当作亲生子看待，而且真心地怜爱，常常抱他。

en.t: Genji not only treated him in public as his own son, but truly loved and cherished him, often taking him in his arms.
